customer_acme_sre: we're seeing 502/timeout errors to the Redwood Private API after we rolled a default-deny egress NetworkPolicy in our workloads namespace. agent logs show repeated TLS handshake failures when contacting the control plane.
TIA_SUPPORT: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a small snippet from the agent pod logs and confirm which k8s CNI (cilium/calico) and kubeproxy mode you're on? also any recent firewall/NAT changes?
customer_acme_sre: cilium, iptables dataplane. no changes to NAT, we did lock down egress to ipv4 only. here's the agent log tail: 
```
2026-02-19T14:02:11Z redwood-agent ERROR dial tcp 34.125.200.11:443: connect: connection refused
2026-02-19T14:02:12Z redwood-agent ERROR tls handshake failed: EOF
2026-02-19T14:02:13Z redwood-agent WARN retrying outbound control-plane connection
```
ops-bot: alert: redwood-private-controlplane: increased 502 rate for customer acme-corp (p95 latency > 2s) :rotating_light:
TIA_SUPPORT: thanks. two likely issues: (1) DNS or egress allowlist blocking, (2) cluster NetworkPolicy preventing node/pod egress to Redwood control plane IP(s). can you exec into the agent pod and run these quick checks?

- `cat /etc/resolv.conf`
- `nslookup control-plane.redwood-inference.com`
- `kubectl exec -n redwood-agent <agent-pod> -- curl -v https://control-plane.redwood-inference.com/health`

If nslookup fails, it's DNS. If curl can't connect but DNS resolves, it's egress blocked.
customer_acme_sre: ran them. dns resolves to 34.125.200.11 and 34.125.200.12. `curl -v` shows "connect: connection refused". `tcpdump` on node shows outgoing SYNs but no replies. looks like our NP is denying egress.
LUCY_INFRA: quick note — K8s NetworkPolicy is by-pod and typically can't match FQDNs. if you're using a default-deny egress you must allow either the control plane CIDRs or the cluster NAT gateway's external IPs. example workaround: allow egress to our control plane IPs/443, or let the node NAT / internet-egress CIDR through. sample NetworkPolicy snippet: 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-controlplane-egress
  namespace: redwood-agent
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 34.125.200.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
TIA_SUPPORT: also verify any cloud firewall/NACL rules between your nodes and the internet. If you're using an egress allowlist at the org level, add control-plane IPs or the FQDN. Redwood control plane uses TLS on 443 only — no special ports required for control channel.
customer_acme_sre: we added the ipBlock /24 to the agent namespace egress and rolled it. within ~30s agent reconnected and requests cleared. p95 latency back to normal. logs show TLS handshake success now. :tada:
SAM_CSE: great, thanks for confirming. for longer term we recommend one of: (1) allow the control-plane CIDR(s) in your egress policy, (2) route outbound to the internet via a NAT gateway IP and allow that IP in your global allowlist, or (3) use an HTTP proxy that the agent can reach and that proxies to redwood (agent supports proxy via env vars).
TIA_SUPPORT: filing a quick KB note so other customers with default-deny NP hits this pattern. thanks for the fast triage, customer_acme_sre. feel free to ping if anything flares up. :thumbsup:
